entry.title: AI;DR: Writer advocates ignoring unedited AI-generated content to encourage human review and editing in professional communication [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: A pro-AI writer expresses frustration with unfiltered AI-generated text being shared without human review, coining the term AI;DR (AI; Didn't Read) as a policy to skip reading such content. The writer emphasizes the importance of editing AI output, especially in professional settings like Slack discussions and newsletters, to maintain quality and clarity. While acknowledging AI's role in tasks like customer support, the writer urges colleagues to prioritize a human touch when sharing AI-assisted writing to ensure effective communication.

entry.title: Qwen3.8 27B scores 52 on Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, outperforming median models with free pricing and 256k token context window [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Qwen3.8 27B, an open weights AI model released in August 2026, achieved a score of 52 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, significantly above the median score of 9 for comparable models. It supports text and image inputs, outputs text, and offers a large 256k token context window, making it one of the leading models in intelligence and cost efficiency among open weight models of similar size. The model generated 160 million tokens during evaluation, indicating high verbosity compared to the median of 43 million tokens. Pricing for Qwen3.8 27B is set at zero dollars per million input and output tokens, making it competitively priced relative to the median costs of $0.04 and $0.15 respectively. The evaluation includes various intelligence benchmarks such as reasoning, coding, and knowledge tasks, positioning Qwen3.8 27B as a strong performer in its class.

entry.title: Wiz Research finds AI-generated GitHub Copilot autofix introduced critical script injection vulnerability in Snowflake's Jira workflow, patched same day [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Wiz Research's AI-powered security tool discovered a critical script injection vulnerability in Snowflake's public GitHub repository, introduced by a GitHub Copilot autofix commit five days earlier. The flaw allowed unauthenticated users to execute arbitrary commands in a GitHub Actions runner by submitting a specially crafted issue title, exposing Jira credentials. Snowflake promptly patched the vulnerability and rotated the affected credentials on the day of disclosure, June 23, 2026. Audit logs confirmed no unauthorized access beyond the security research team's proof-of-concept testing, which involved exfiltrating base64-encoded Jira tokens to demonstrate the exploit.

entry.title: Guide details how to disable or avoid intrusive AI features across popular software and devices [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: A comprehensive guide explains how users can disable or avoid intrusive AI features in various software and devices, including Adobe Acrobat, Android phones with Gemini, Apple devices with Apple Intelligence and Siri, and major web browsers like Chrome, Edge, Firefox, and DuckDuckGo. The guide targets users who prefer less AI interference in their technology environments and provides step-by-step instructions for turning off AI functionalities. The guide also covers disabling AI enhancements in Google Workspace applications such as Gmail and Google Docs, and offers tips for managing AI-related settings to reduce unwanted AI interactions. It is intended as a resource for users seeking more control over AI features integrated into everyday technology.

entry.title: OpenAI releases GPT-5.6 Sol, its strongest vision model with significant improvements in object detection and counting [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: OpenAI introduced the GPT-5.6 lineup, including the Sol, Terra, and Luna models, with Sol demonstrating the best vision capabilities to date. The models showed notable progress in tasks like object detection, counting, OCR, and data extraction, with Sol outperforming previous versions and competitors in several benchmarks. Sol achieved a substantial jump in object detection accuracy, scoring 46.2 mAP@50 compared to GPT-5.5's 13.8, and improved counting accuracy to 73.0%. While OCR performance remained close to GPT-5.5, Sol excelled in complex visual scenes and document layout detection. Some stability issues were noted with large images, which OpenAI acknowledged and suggested resizing as a workaround.

entry.title: Researchers present a zero-overhead GPU offload framework integrated into Rust compiler, enabling portable, safe, and fast GPU programming across multiple vendors
entry.summary: Researchers have developed a GPU offload framework built directly into the Rust compiler and LLVM backends that aims to combine high performance with Rust's compile-time memory safety guarantees. This framework addresses challenges in cross-vendor ABI compatibility and uses Rust's ownership and type systems to optimize data transfers and memory management for GPU kernels. Evaluations on RAJAPerf benchmarks show that the Rust-based solution generates LLVM IR competitive with native CUDA and HIP C++ implementations, demonstrating solid kernel performance without sacrificing safety or portability. The approach avoids vendor lock-in and explicit unsafe code, potentially broadening Rust's applicability in high-performance GPU programming.

entry.title: Speko launches OpenRouter for Voice AI, providing a unified API that routes speech models by language and objective based on benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Speko has introduced an OpenRouter for Voice AI that integrates multiple speech models into a single API, selecting the best model per language and task using published performance measurements rather than vendor leaderboards. The platform offers a unified gateway with one base URL and API key, compatible with existing frameworks like LiveKit, Pipecat, and Claude, enabling developers to run and monitor voice AI agents efficiently. The service benchmarks speech models across languages and evaluates them by score versus cost at different stages, allowing users to optimize voice AI workflows. Speko's API speaks the OpenAI protocol, making it easy to integrate with current tools by simply pointing agents to Speko's gateway without changing existing agent code.

entry.title: Fast.ai co-founder returns to AI startup Answer.AI to focus on ethical AI in education amid widespread criticism and misuse of AI technologies [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: The co-founder of fast.ai has announced a return to the AI field by joining Answer.AI, an AI startup focused on ethical applications in education. Despite widespread criticism of AI's negative impacts on education, open-source projects, and misinformation, the founder aims to develop AI tools that preserve human judgment and critical thinking. The founder previously left AI due to burnout and concerns over the industry's direction, including overhyped claims and resource misuse. Answer.AI's SolveIt tool emphasizes human control and iterative problem-solving, countering trends of AI-generated content that undermine learning and creativity. This return reflects a commitment to responsible AI development amid growing public backlash and ethical challenges.

entry.title: Flock updates police license plate reader platform to curb misuse amid stalking cases but critics highlight loopholes and privacy concerns
entry.summary: Flock, a police technology company operating around 120,000 automatic license plate readers across the US, announced platform changes aimed at preventing illegal or illegitimate use, including stalking by officers. These updates require officers to enter a criminal case number for searches and use software to flag abnormal activity, responding to reports of misuse such as stalking and harassment. However, the new measures have significant loopholes, including the ability for officers to enter false case numbers, and do not address broader civil liberties concerns about mass surveillance. Critics argue that Flock's system design choices-such as data collection scope, search permissions, and data retention policies-set problematic terms for balancing security and privacy. The company's business model depends on maintaining a large, interconnected network, which some cities and states are pushing back against through contract cancellations and proposed legislation.

entry.title: Anthropic's annualized revenue surges to $65 billion by July, up from $9 billion at end of 2025 [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Anthropic, an AI model developer, has rapidly increased its annualized revenue run rate to $65 billion by the end of July 2026, up from $9 billion at the end of 2025. This growth outpaces rival OpenAI, which doubled its revenue to $40 billion over the same period. Investors expect Anthropic's revenue to reach between $100 billion and $120 billion by the end of 2026. The company is preparing for a public offering possibly as soon as this fall, aiming for a valuation of $2 trillion or more, which would set a record for the largest market debut.

Despite having only 27 billion parameters, Qwen 3.8 27B performs comparably to much larger models, including GLM-5.2 with 753 billion parameters and DeepSeek with 1.6 billion parameters. This result highlights Qwen 3.8 27B as a notable model in generative AI and large language model development.

entry.title: Smolbox runs a full x86_64 Linux VM with integrated LLM AI entirely in a browser tab using WebAssembly and WebGPU [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Smolbox is a proof-of-concept virtual machine sandbox that operates fully within a web browser tab, running Alpine Linux on an x86_64 VM via WebAssembly. It integrates a large language model (LLM) AI using WebGPU, allowing AI tool calls inside the VM without any server-side processing, and supports mounting user-selected files read-only into the VM. The project demonstrates that complex AI and VM environments can run client-side, highlighting potential for agentic AI use without centralized servers. The creator reflects on past experiences with limited internet access and discusses challenges teenagers face today in accessing AI tools on locked-down devices or without payment methods, emphasizing the resourcefulness required to overcome such barriers.

entry.title: AI automation startup Relay shuts down; founder Jacob Bank and staff join Google Chrome team to advance AI integration [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Relay, an AI-powered workflow automation startup launched in 2021, is shutting down its service with paid customer access ending September 14 and free access already terminated. Founder and CEO Jacob Bank, who previously worked at Google, is rejoining the company as VP of Product for Google Chrome, where he will lead product and developer relations teams. Relay aimed to streamline repetitive business tasks through automation, similar to Zapier, but will now see its team contribute to Google's Chrome browser. Bank indicated plans to enhance AI capabilities within Chrome, describing it as an ideal platform for collaboration with AI agents, aligning with Google's broader integration of AI technologies like Gemini into its products.

entry.title: Un-AI Your Internet: A guide to reducing reliance on AI-driven tools and services online [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: The article critiques the widespread integration of large language models and AI technologies in internet services, arguing that current AI implementations are inefficient simulations rather than true intelligence. It advocates for users to actively remove or disable AI features from their devices and software to regain control over their online experience. It outlines practical steps such as avoiding AI-heavy platforms like Google Search and Chrome, and choosing alternatives that do not bundle AI, emphasizing the tension between user freedom and the controlled environments promoted by major tech companies. The article warns that AI's pervasive presence is driven by heavy investments and may be difficult to avoid, but encourages users to resist supporting AI-dependent products and services where possible.

entry.title: Rysh launches an AI-powered terminal multiplexer in Go, enabling Claude and Codex agents to collaborate in multiple panes with session persistence and local secret management [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Rysh has released an agentic terminal multiplexer written in Go that allows multiple AI agents, including Claude and Codex, to operate simultaneously in separate panes within a single session. Each pane acts as an independent agent capable of answering prompts and executing tasks, with sessions persisting state even after restarts. The tool supports complex workflows where agents can coordinate tasks, such as managing project goals and parallel work orders, all within a familiar terminal interface. The software ensures security by substituting secrets with tokens before requests leave the local machine, preventing exposure of sensitive data to the AI models. Rysh is available as open-source software under the Apache-2.0 license and supports macOS, Linux, and Windows via WSL2. It offers both source builds and prebuilt binaries, with detailed documentation and video tutorials to guide users through its features and installation.

The platform supports two modes: a managed cloud service with Kubernetes pods running multi-hop tool-calling loops via the OpenAI Responses API, and a Bring Your Own Agent (BYOA) option allowing users to run agents locally with their own AI subscriptions.

entry.title: Will Anthropic and OpenAI Stop Selling Their Best AI to Businesses? [ * ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Anthropic and OpenAI's move to develop AI applications and features tailored to specific industries continues to worry their customers, some of which must now compete head-on with their main AI suppliers. Design app Canva is the latest to find itself in this predicament, as we reported earlier this month. Through it all, though, most people assumed Anthropic and OpenAI would always offer their models through an application programming interface, which is a multibillion-dollar revenue driver for both of them. As long as it stays that way, businesses will stand a chance against the new competition. But will it? Conversations I've had in recent weeks with researchers at these frontier labs and founders whose applications depend on the latest models left me wondering if the status quo will persist.

entry.title: Arm CFO Eyes Deals as Chip Building Bring New Challenges [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Arm shares have more than doubled this year as the U.K. company has benefited from demand for the central processing units it designs and a new AI chip it is selling. And that soaring share price has given the SoftBank-controlled company, now worth $300 billion, more firepower to do acquisitions. In the past, Arm has mostly made small purchases, such as last year's $265 million deal for networking startup DreamBig. It's likely to stick to this kind of acquisition in the future, Arm Chief Financial Officer Jason Child said in an interview. But he indicated the company hasn't ruled out bigger ones. That's especially the case as its decision to sell its own chips, not just license its designs to companies like Nvidia and Apple, forces it to grapple with new growth and the challenges that come with it. "Delivering silicon is definitely more complicated" than licensing designs, he said.

entry.title: We Tracked a Shipment of Rare Books. It Ended at an Amazon AI Training Facility [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: We Tracked a Shipment of Rare Books. It Ended at an Amazon AI Training Facility Excellent piece of reporting from 404 Media. For a while now there have been stories of book dealers receiving orders for large volumes of books from apparently price-insensitive anonymous customers, widely suspected to be companies looking to scan them for AI training (see my previous coverage of Anthropic's book scanning from June 2025.) 404 Media investigated with an AirTag! In July, one bookseller told me they received a very large order of around 1,000 books on Biblio, one of these marketplaces. The seller agreed to put an Apple AirTag provided by 404 Media in one of the books included in this order so we could see where the book was going. And by extension, which company, AI or otherwise, was behind this massive order. The book ended up delivered to the VGT3 corner of the LAS8 Amazon facility in the north east of Las Vegas, where the entrance carried this on-the-nose logo of a dinosaur with a book! Photo credit: 404 Media Online forum discussions between Amazon workers confirmed that VGT3 destructively scans large volumes of books. Tags: amazon, journalism, ai, training-data, ai-ethics, 404-media
